questions.q: What does reputation management software do?
questions.a: Reputation management software tracks what people say about your business and helps you respond. Good tools monitor mentions across review sites, social media, press and forums, pull reviews into one inbox and help you reply quickly with AI-assisted drafts. They also measure sentiment by location, topic and time so you can turn feedback into action.

questions.q: When does a business need reputation management software?
questions.a: You usually feel the need once you run more than one location. Reviews pile up across many platforms with no central place to track them, replying to each one becomes a full-time job, and it gets hard to tell what customers really think. Software brings those reviews together and makes the work manageable.

questions.q: Is review management the same as reputation management?
questions.a: Review management is one part of reputation management. Reputation management also covers social listening, listings accuracy, surveys and, for some companies, how investors, employees and other stakeholders see the brand. Pick tools based on which of these you actually need to track.

questions.q: How much does reputation management software cost?
questions.a: Costs range from simple monthly plans for small businesses to custom enterprise contracts priced by location or customer interactions. Several platforms don't publish pricing and ask you to contact sales. Per-user pricing on social tools can add up quickly for larger teams, so count users as well as locations.

questions.q: What should a multi-location brand look for in reputation management software?
questions.a: Look for three things: it unifies reviews from all platforms and locations, responds to reviews at scale, and surfaces insights about guest experience and operations. Location-level dashboards and benchmarking help you spot which stores need attention. Approval workflows matter if replies need sign-off before they're published.

questions.q: Which reputation management software is built for restaurants?
questions.a: Momos is built for multi-location restaurants and hospitality businesses. It brings reviews, social messages, surveys and delivery platform feedback from every location into one Unified Inbox, where its AI agent Alfie writes on-brand replies. Its analytics show what drives positive and negative reviews and where incidents happen most.
